chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But upon those who take him as their guardian.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/master

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority (hukm) is not absolute over all believers but is conditional upon their voluntary submission, distinguishing between those who follow his whispers and those who remain steadfast in faith. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (ikhtiyar), where Satan acts as a clear guide (hujjah) rather than an irresistible compeller, reinforcing the idea that spiritual success depends on conscious choice rather than divine predestination of evil.
